reference: LibreOffice 26.8 PDF export of each DOCX/ODT, rasterized by the extension's pdf.js reader
rationale: Pages are compared as grids of ~1.2 mm cells holding mean ink (darkness), measured on the full-resolution page images of both renderers.

match: F1 of reference/rendered ink cells that have ink of the other side within matchRadius cells (3 = ~3.7 mm); tolerates font substitution and small shifts, drops when content is missing, extra or moved.

rows / columns: Pearson correlation of the smoothed row and column ink profiles; rows drops when vertical rhythm (line spacing, page breaks) drifts, columns when widths or horizontal placement change.
coverage: smaller / larger total ink; drops when content, images or shading are lost or added.

gutters: agreement of wide vertical gaps (columns, text beside pictures, table cells, tab stops) found in sliding windows of gutterBand rows; catches lost columns or wrapping that leave the amount of ink unchanged.
aspect: page shape ratio; a wrong page size or orientation, or a page extended by overflowing content, falls below 0.98.

Defaults were set from the pages that render like LibreOffice (tables-styled.docx, table-long.docx, landscape-sections.docx, math-formula.docx and the unaffected pages of other files score match >= 0.95, rows >= 0.85, columns >= 0.95, coverage >= 0.9, gutters >= 0.85), with headroom for font substitution.

A file below the defaults is listed as a known difference with its reason; its own minimums are the observed values minus 0.05, so the check still fails if it gets worse. Observed values are recorded for reference.

odt.knownDifference: Page 1 ends with a single justified line of a split paragraph (no fo:widows in the corpus style, as in LibreOffice); the descenders of the line above fall into the last 3 cm measuring window, which then holds only that line, and its word gaps count as gutters (11 band-cells against a floor of 30). The text, line positions and page breaks match (match 1.0, rows 0.97).

Page 3 holds one or two rows fewer or more than LibreOffice's: row heights differ by a fraction of a pixel per row (Liberation fonts and cell padding rounding), which adds up over a 70-row table, so the last page carries a different number of rows and its ink coverage differs. Header repetition, widths and shading match.

LibreOffice keeps the 12 x 8 cm chart (wrap none, style:flow-with-text="false") on page 1 hanging into the bottom margin and, because the chart then covers the last line of the paragraph above, moves that one line ("the persistent fog.") to page 2; the extension also hangs the chart into the margin but keeps the line on page 1, so page 2 starts one line higher. Small bitmaps scaled up are smoothed by Chromium, while pdf.js draws them with sharp pixels.

Page 2: the last body line is a split, fully justified line just above the footer; the descenders of the line before it fall into the same 3 cm measuring window as the footer, and the gaps between the justified words and around "Page 2 of 3" count as gutters on our side only. Header and footer tab stops, the different first page and the page fields match (match 1.0, rows 0.97).

Formulas are typeset by Chromium MathML instead of LibreOffice Math: about 20% smaller and spaced differently (content complete), so the text after each formula sits higher. Gutters: as in math-formula.docx, the last short line of the page shares its measuring window with the descenders of the line above.

docx.knownDifference: The last line of the page ("ended.") shares the last 3 cm measuring window with only the descenders of the line above, so the empty width beside it counts as gutters on our side (a metric artifact since the 1.15 DOCX line-height factor moved the text by a pixel); match 0.996, rows 0.995 and columns 0.997 show the page itself matches. Formulas are typeset by Chromium MathML, with wider operator spacing than LibreOffice's.

odt.knownDifference: LibreOffice also wraps the title paragraph above the anchor paragraph around the paragraph-anchored "Tip" frame (its title breaks onto two lines), which pushes everything below down by one title line; the extension wraps only the anchor paragraph and the ones after it. The frame position, fill, outline and the full-width notice match.
